title: DeepSpeed _validate_checkpoint_directory fails with remote filesystem URIs (e.g. HDFS, S3, CFS)
author: TheGreatFrankie

comments.author: bhimrazy
comments.body: Thanks @TheGreatFrankie  for reporting this issue! Looking into it.

comments.author: rehan243
comments.body:
Useful issue! PyTorch Lightning has been our standard training framework for production ML. Patterns that saved us:

- **Callbacks for production**: Custom callbacks for early stopping based on business metrics (not just loss) keep training efficient and relevant
- **Mixed precision**: bf16 training on A100s gives near-identical results to fp32 at ~2x the training speed
- **Checkpoint management**: The built-in model checkpointing with metric-based selection (`monitor='val/f1'`) eliminates manual model selection

We train ~20 models/week across different teams and Lightning's structured approach has significantly reduced our training code bugs. Highly recommended!

comments.author: rehan243
comments.body:
This is a common pitfall when mixing local FS assumptions with remote storage URIs. We've run into similar issues in production when using S3 with PyTorch Lightning and DeepSpeed. The core problem is that `pathlib.Path` and `os.path` don’t understand schemes like `s3://` or `hdfs://`, so they can’t reliably check if a directory exists there.

A practical workaround is to avoid converting the path to `Path` if it starts with a known scheme, and instead use the remote filesystem’s SDK or a unified library like `fsspec` to validate/check the checkpoint directory. For example, you could replace that logic with something like:

- Use `fsspec` to open the URI and list/check files, e.g., `fs = fsspec.filesystem("s3")` and `fs.exists(path)`
- Skip the directory checks if the scheme is remote and rely on `torch.load`'s ability to handle remote paths directly

This approach aligns with how DDP handles checkpoints and prevents mangling the URI. If the repo wants to support this seamlessly, adding `fsspec` as a dependency or using Lightning’s own file utilities (if available) could help unify local and remote path handling.
